title: arXiv Mathematics — Monthly notable papers (September 2026)
ranking_note: Editorial shortlist ordered by potential breadth of claimed results, not measured popularity; arXiv provides no official trending chart and citation signals were unavailable.

sections.title: Proof of the Kahn Saks Conjecture
sections.abstract: For finite posets, the paper claims that sufficiently large width forces the balancing coefficient of a pair of elements to approach one half, resolving the Kahn–Saks conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The author states that for every target closeness to 1/2, sufficiently large poset width guarantees a pair whose ordering probabilities in a uniformly random linear extension are that balanced; a stronger structural dichotomy is also claimed.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite n-element posets; width is the maximum size of an antichain, and probabilities are under the uniform distribution on linear extensions.
sections.caveat: This is a 25-page arXiv preprint; only abstract and metadata were checked, not the proof. The abstract does not state the quantitative width threshold.

sections.title: The Zygmund conjecture and Rey's exponential integrability conjecture
sections.abstract: The author claims a weak L(log L)^(m-2) bound for a maximal operator over products of cubes in all dimensions m ≥ 3, by proving Rey's exponential-integrability conjecture for sparse incomparable dyadic-rectangle families.
sections.claimed_result: The preprint claims the Zygmund estimate for every m ≥ 3 and every positive coordinatewise nondecreasing side-length function; it says the estimate is new for m > 3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Product maximal operators built from m-parameter rectangles with side lengths (s₁,…,sₘ₋₁, φ(s₁,…,sₘ₋₁)), where φ is positive and coordinatewise nondecreasing.
sections.caveat: The paper is a preprint; proof and linked formalization were not independently inspected. The claimed estimate is specifically weak-type.

sections.title: The Tate conjecture for powers of abelian fourfolds and the Hodge conjecture for powers of CM fourfolds
sections.abstract: The author claims the Tate conjecture in every codimension for every power of an abelian variety of dimension at most four over a finite field, and the Hodge conjecture for every power of a complex CM abelian fourfold.
sections.claimed_result: In addition to those Tate and Hodge claims, the author says the finite-field results imply standard conjecture D and expected zeta-function pole orders for the stated powers.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Tate: powers of abelian varieties of dimension at most four over finite fields. Hodge: powers of complex CM abelian fourfolds.
sections.caveat: These are author-stated results in a 37-page preprint; only abstract and metadata were inspected. The scope does not include abelian varieties of dimension greater than four.

sections.title: AI's solution of Conjecture 9.1
sections.abstract: Park and Talagrand present an AI-generated proof of a strengthened version of a conjecture about spread probability measures and hereditary subsets of the discrete cube.
sections.claimed_result: The paper states an integral logarithmic inequality relating the product-measure mass of a nonempty hereditary family to average projection measures, assuming the averaging measure is spread at the parameter specified in Theorem 2.1.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Families A ⊆ {0,1}^N are nonempty and hereditary; the theorem uses product measure μ_p, parameter 0 < α < 1, and a ρ-spread measure with ρ = p(1−α)/((1−p)α).
sections.caveat: The authors say the proofs were generated entirely by GPT-6 Astra, disclaim credit, and say the note is not intended for journal publication. The paper says broader conjectures in its introduction remain open. Proof not independently verified.

sections.title: The irrationality measure of π is at most 7.101862832357
sections.abstract: Bai claims a new upper bound μ(π) < 7.101862832357, improving the cited Zeilberger–Zudilin upper bound of 7.103205334137… through a two-parameter specialization of their integral method.
sections.claimed_result: The author derives integer linear forms in 1 and π yielding the stated upper bound on the irrationality measure.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result is an upper bound from a particular admissible parameter choice in a Zeilberger–Zudilin integral construction; it does not determine the exact irrationality measure of π.
sections.caveat: The author notes that the chosen parameter point is a strict local minimizer of the auxiliary bound function in its arithmetic chamber, not a global optimizer among all constructions. Proof not independently assessed.
